title: Latency-driven region scorer with asymmetric p50/p95 weighting and link-quality escrow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a region scoring service that synthesizes latency percentiles (p50 and p95) with link-quality signals into a single, explainable score to drive region selection and variant fallback. Unlike prior approaches that treated p50 and p95 symmetrically, this design intentionally biases toward p50 for typical latency preference but applies an asymmetric multiplicative penalty for p95 regressions to protect tail-sensitive customers. In addition, a link-quality escrow mechanism temporarily holds routing decisions for regions exhibiting volatile packet loss or path flapping so we avoid oscillation across short-lived network events.
decision_summary: Choose an additive baseline score derived from expected p50 latency, then apply a multiplicative p95 penalty factor scaled by the p95/p50 ratio and a link-stability escrow multiplier derived from packet-loss and retransmit-rate EWMA. Final score is lower-is-better; routing picks region with minimal score after accounting for affinity and capacity slack. We will also maintain a short-lived routing cache (10s) to reduce churn and use hysteresis for region eviction.
scoring_formula: score = base_ms + (alpha * p50_ms) + beta * (p95_ms - p50_ms) * max(1, p95/p50) * link_penalty; link_penalty = 1 + gamma * clipped(packet_loss_ewma,0,0.2) + delta * clipped(retransmits_ewma,0,0.2)
implementation_tasks: instrument telemetry aggregation job to emit region-level p50/p95 and packet loss EWMA (ENG-520001)
build region-scorer microservice (go) with configurable alpha/beta/gamma/delta and runtime flags
extend router to consult scorer with timeout and fallback to cached decision on scorer failure
add binding table mapping model variants to region capabilities (e.g., full->quantized->edge-cached)
create canary feature flag and rollout pipeline in Console for per-customer steering
add dashboards and SLI alerts for scoring anomalies and increased decision churn
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal staging region with synthetic traffic, verify scoring outputs and canary flag controls (1 day). Stage 2: roll to 1% of traffic in staging customer cohort for 48 hours, monitor p95 regressions and failover behavior (3 days). Stage 3: progressive ramp (1%->5%->25%->100%) over 2 weeks with automated rollback on defined SLO breaches. Use kill-switch in Console to revert to existing percentile-only routing.
acceptance_criteria: Scorer exposes documented score and contributing signals via /metrics and traces
On canary, region decisions respect configured alpha/beta within tolerance and are stable (median churn < 0.5 decisions/min per POP)
During 25% pilot, platform p95 tail violations do not increase beyond historical variance (within 2 standard deviations)
Link-escrow prevents oscillation: regions with packet_loss_ewma > 0.05 retain traffic hold for configured escrow window (default 30s) and show reduced flip-rate
Fallback mapping correctly routes traffic to compatible model variant when primary region is penalized, with no more than 1% of requests experiencing higher-variance outputs in pilot
open_questions: What default alpha/beta/gamma/delta give best empirical tradeoff across enterprise vs PLG workloads? We will A/B tune but need safe defaults.
Should we weight p95 penalties by SLA tier (enterprise customers get stricter p95 protection)?
How long should the routing cache/hysteresis window be for regional decisions across short-lived spikes? 10s initial, but may need tuning.
Edge cases: how to handle regions with sparse telemetry (cold start)? Proposed: fall back to synthetic probe latency and regional historical baseline.
What observability surface is required for SRE to quickly diagnose scorer regressions? (logs, traces, scoring breakdown in Console)
